Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) Second Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan II) (c. 600 AD)

**OPENS Ch 16: ANTI-SAMARITAN RESURRECTION-DENIAL POLEMIC** (vv. 1-7) — the chapter develops the Samaritan-error specifically (named-but-not-developed at seed 14:1). The Samaritans' specific error per Meqabyan: REJECTION OF ALL SCRIPTURE BEYOND THE PENTATEUCH, hence rejection of the prophetic-eschatological-resurrection-doctrine that depends on Daniel 12 + Isaiah 26 + Ezekiel 37. Historical-Samaritan-doctrine per Josephus + early-patristic-witnesses (Origen Contra Celsum 1.49; Epiphanius Panarion 9) confirms the Pentateuch-only canon and the consequent resurrection-denial-or-uncertainty. The Meqabyan polemic argues from PENTATEUCH-ITSELF for resurrection (the Christ-with-Sadducees argumentation pattern at Matthew 22:31-32 par. — 'God is not the God of the dead, but of the living' citing Exodus 3:6 'the God of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob'). Per CROSS_REFERENCE_APPENDIX §44: the anti-Samaritan polemic is one of Meqabyan's most historically-specific theological engagements — locating the text in the Tewahedo-tradition's awareness of Samaritan-textual-tradition.

GERIZIM / TABERNACLE-TRADITION CRITIQUE (vv. 8-14): the Meqabyan polemic against Samaritan-Gerizim-temple-tradition. Mount Gerizim is the Samaritan alternative-Temple-location (vs Jerusalem) per the Samaritan-Pentateuch's altered Deuteronomy 27:4 reading (EBAL → GERIZIM textual-shift) and the Samaritan-Temple history (built ca. 4th c. BCE, destroyed by Hyrcanus ca. 110 BCE per Josephus Antiquities 13.9.1). Direct biblical parallel: JOHN 4:19-26 (the Samaritan-woman-at-the-well — 'Our fathers worshipped in this mountain; and ye say, that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship'; Christ's response: 'salvation is of the Jews... the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth'). The Meqabyan critique echoes the Johannine Jewish-priority-of-cultic-place-but-true-worship-spiritualized logic. Tewahedo liturgical-tradition preserves the awareness of Gerizim-vs-Jerusalem controversy in its Säʿatat (Liturgy of the Hours) Psalter recitation of psalms-of-Zion.
